medical.name: Doctors and medical centres
medical.desc: General practices, medical specialists, urgent care and medical centres
profile: Number of doctors and nurse practitioners
Surgical or invasive procedures carried out?

pi: Procedures and scope
Cosmetic procedures, minor surgery and new services can fall outside the usual policy. Ask about every procedure performed and the practitioner’s training.
Medical records and consent
Poor notes and consent records make claims harder to defend. Ask about record systems and consent processes.
cyber: Health records are highly sensitive. A breach brings notification duties under the Privacy Act 2020 and the Health Information Privacy Code. Check cyber limits and response support.

dental.name: Dentists
dental.desc: Dental practices, orthodontists and dental technicians
profile: Digital X-ray and CBCT equipment owned?

gen: Equipment values and breakdown
Chairs, X-ray, CBCT, sterilisation and IT. Check replacement values, breakdown cover and the time to replace specialist equipment.
pi: Implants, sedation and complex work
Higher-risk procedures draw higher claims. Check the limit and any exclusions for sedation, cosmetic dentistry and overseas practitioners.
bi: A closed practice loses chair income while staff costs continue. Check gross profit, indemnity period and cover for locum or alternative premises.

alliedhealth.name: Physios, chiropractors and allied health
alliedhealth.desc: Physiotherapy, chiropractic, osteopathy, massage, counselling and podiatry
profile: Spinal manipulation or high-velocity techniques used?

pi: Treatment risks
Manipulation, dry needling and deep tissue work can cause injury. ACC covers most treatment injury, but check defence costs, complaints cover and exclusions.
Counselling and boundaries
Allegations of misconduct or advice complaints. Check cover for disciplinary and complaints investigation costs.

pharmacy.name: Pharmacies
profile: Robbery or burglary incidents in the last 5 years?

gen: Controlled drugs and security
Safes, alarm response, procedures after hours and staff safety. Thefts of controlled drugs are common.
pi: Dispensing errors
Wrong drug, wrong dose or missed interaction. Check professional indemnity limits, locum cover and dispensing procedures.
mdamage: Vaccines and refrigerated medicines. Check breakdown cover, alarms and the limit for loss of stock.

vet.name: Veterinary clinics
vet.desc: Small animal and large animal veterinary practices
profile: Boarding, grooming or hospitalisation of animals?

pi: Treatment and surgery claims
Animal death, wrong procedure or misdiagnosis. ACC does not cover animals, so claims are not barred. Check the limit, sentimental-value claims and any exclusions.
Large animal and racehorse work
High-value animals and stud work raise claim values. Check the limit against the largest animal treated.
liab: Animals in your care
Pets and livestock boarded or hospitalised, and escapes. Check care, custody and control cover.

agedcare.name: Rest homes and care providers
agedcare.desc: Rest homes, home care, disability and community support services
profile: Falls, pressure injuries or medication incidents recorded and reviewed?
Share of staff who are agency or casual (%)

gen: Resident safety and incident trends
Falls, pressure injuries, medication errors and restraint use. Underwriters ask for incident trends and corrective actions.
liab: Resident property and wandering
Residents’ belongings, absconding residents and abuse allegations. Check care, custody and control cover and defence costs.
mdamage: Evacuation of residents who cannot move quickly. Check sprinklers, evacuation scheme, staffing at night and building warrant of fitness.
dno: Trustees, directors and managers. Check employment practices and regulatory investigation cover.

ece.name: Preschools and childcare
ece.desc: Early childhood education: preschools, kindergartens, daycare, playcentres, kōhanga reo
profile: Water play, paddling pools or access to a pool?
Share of income from Ministry of Education funding (%)
Notifiable incidents or complaints to the Ministry in the last 3 years?

liab: ec_abuse
Abuse cover on the current policy
opt
ec_gate
Gates and fencing secure, with sign-in and sign-out of children?
yn
mdamage: Toys, furniture and learning resources value

gen: Licensing and compliance
Current licence, the latest Education Review Office report and any Ministry action. Non-compliance can lead to suspension, which is a business interruption event.
Structure and governance
Who is the licence holder: a company, trust or society? Directors and committee members are personally exposed, so consider management liability cover.
Funding dependence
Ministry funding and fee income. What happens to income if the centre closes for a few weeks?
Staffing and ratios
Use of relievers and casual staff, and how ratios are met at the start and end of the day.
liab: Duty of care and supervision
Injury is mostly covered by ACC, but claims for defence costs, exemplary damages and property still arise. Check what the policy responds to.
Outings and transport
Trips on foot, bus hire, parent drivers and staff vehicles. Child restraints, driver licence checks and written parent consent.
Water, food and allergies
Pools, paddling pools, beach trips, food prepared on site and allergy action plans.
Playground safety
Equipment inspected to the NZ playground standard, soft-fall surfaces and a record of incidents.
statutory: Education regulations, health and safety, Privacy Act and Children’s Act obligations. Check defence cost cover. Fines under health and safety law cannot be insured.
pi: Professional indemnity
Claims arising from advice, assessments, learning plans and from records and reports about children and families.
dno: Volunteer committee members and trustees. Check past and present members, spouses and employment practices cover.
mdamage: Owned or leased, who insures the building, and the value of playgrounds, fencing and shade structures. Earthquake-prone status and heating or electrical condition for older buildings.
Toys, books, furniture, kitchens, laundry and IT. Ask for an asset list and when it was last updated.
bi: Gross revenue includes fees and Ministry funding. Consider how long it takes to repair or find premises and re-open, and extra costs for temporary premises.
crime: Who handles fees and cash, dual authorisation on payments, and fraud by an employee or volunteer treasurer.
cyber: Enrolment records, photos and health information. A breach brings notification duties under the Privacy Act 2020. Check photo and consent practices.
fleet: Vans or minibuses: driver licences, passenger endorsements, child restraints and maintenance records.

education.name: Schools and training providers
education.desc: Private schools, tertiary and training providers, tutors, driving schools
profile: Field trips, camps or adventure activities?
Share of income from government funding (%)
Practical or trade training with machinery or tools?

gen: Regulatory approvals
Registration and quality assurance with the relevant education regulator. Loss of registration can stop operations.
International students
Pastoral care code obligations, student welfare and refund exposure on closure. Check relevant cover.
liab: Trips, camps and adventure activities
Injury is covered by ACC but defence costs, property loss and exemplary damages still arise. Check exclusions for adventure activities and transport.
Practical training
Machinery and workshop training raise injury and property exposure. Ask about supervision and instructor qualifications.
pi: Educational outcomes and certification
Claims over qualifications, assessments or advice. Check cover for loss of accreditation and refunds.

fitness.name: Gyms, fitness and recreation
fitness.desc: Gyms, personal trainers, yoga, sports clubs, swimming and recreation operators
profile: Personal training or classes led by staff and contractors?
Pool, sauna or spa on site?
High-risk activities such as climbing, boxing or contact sport?

liab: Participant injury and waivers
ACC covers most injury, but check defence costs, exemplary damages and property damage. Waivers do not remove exposure for negligence.
Trainers and instructors
Qualifications, insurance for contractors and supervision. Check professional indemnity for coaching advice.
mdamage: Equipment values and breakdown cover. Check replacement values and age of cardio equipment.
Pool, sauna and spa plant, chemical storage and water safety.
bi: Direct debit income, memberships paid in advance and the effect of a closure. Check the indemnity period and refund exposure.

beauty.name: Hair, beauty and tattoo studios
beauty.desc: Hairdressers, barbers, beauty salons, day spas, nail and tattoo studios
profile: Staff and chair or booth renters
Laser, IPL or other energy-based devices used?

liab: Treatment reactions and burns
Allergic reactions, chemical burns, laser burns and infections. ACC covers treatment injury, but check defence costs and exclusions for cosmetic injectables and lasers.
Patch testing and consent
Patch tests, consent forms and records are the main defence in a claim. Ask how they are kept.
Chair and booth renters
Self-employed renters may not be covered by your policy. Check agreements and whether each holds their own insurance.
mdamage: Salon fit-out, equipment and retail stock. Check replacement values and theft limits.

cleaning.name: Cleaning and property services
cleaning.desc: Commercial and domestic cleaning, window cleaning, carpet cleaning and property maintenance
profile: Hold customers’ keys or alarm codes?

gen: Key and access control
Lost keys, alarm codes and access to customer premises. Ask about key registers, fobs and re-keying costs, and cover for lost keys.
liab: Damage to customer property and theft allegations
Breakages, floor damage and allegations of theft are the usual claims. Check dishonesty cover for employees and customer-held keys.
Chemicals and pest control
Chemical damage, poisoning and wrongly applied treatments. Check certification, records and pollution exclusions.
crime: Staff dishonesty at customer premises. Check the crime policy extends to customers’ property and the limit.

community.name: Clubs, churches and community groups
community.desc: Sports clubs, churches, charities, trusts, community halls and societies

gen: Volunteers and who is covered
Are volunteers treated as employees for liability purposes? Check personal accident cover for volunteers and cover for committee members.
Events and hire of premises
Fundraisers, fairs and hired halls. Check public liability for events, alcohol and temporary structures.
dno: Committee members and trustees. Check governance, any disputes and cover for historic claims and employment matters.
crime: Dual authorisation on payments and bank reconciliation by a second person. Volunteer treasurers are often alone with the funds.
